purpose.text: Enable OpenClaw agents to search the web through Google's Custom Search API (PSE), supporting live information, documentation lookup, and topic research when built-in web_search is unavailable.

evidences.reason: States the search mechanism, intended information needs, and built-in search availability condition.
Identifies OpenClaw agents as the intended users of the Google Custom Search capability.

requirements.text: Use this skill when live information, documentation, or topic research is needed and built-in web_search is unavailable.

evidences.reason: Explicitly directs use under these information needs and availability conditions, without establishing an exclusive-use prohibition.

requirements.text: Create a project in Google Cloud Console and enable the Custom Search API for that project.

evidences.reason: Requires project creation and API enablement as a connected setup step.
Explicitly requires generating an API key.

requirements.text: Create a Programmable Search Engine at the specified Google CSE site and obtain its CX ID.

evidences.reason: Requires creating the search engine and obtaining the identifier belonging to that engine.

requirements.text: Store the API key and search engine CX ID in a .env file in the workspace, under GOOGLE_API_KEY and GOOGLE_CSE_ID respectively.

evidences.reason: Specifies credential storage location and the names corresponding to the two credential values.

requirements.text: Pass both credentials to the script through environment variables named GOOGLE_API_KEY and GOOGLE_CSE_ID; both must be set for execution.

evidences.reason: Explicitly states that credentials will be passed through environment variables and that both named variables must be set. This runtime requirement can coexist with the separate .env storage requirement.

requirements.text: Supply a search query as the first positional argument when invoking the search script.

evidences.reason: The usage contract requires a query argument, and the script identifies the first positional argument as that query.
